UNESCO site

Ushguli

One of Europe's highest permanently inhabited settlements at 2,100 m, under Mount Shkhara — UNESCO-listed as part of Upper Svaneti.

Time needed
4 h
From Tbilisi
515 km · 10:30
Road
Unpaved sections
Car needed
Off-road 4x4
Season
June–September
Entry
~5 ₾

Ushguli is the collective name for four closely spaced villages — Chazhashi, Chvibiani, Zhibiani and Murqmeli — standing at the head of the Enguri valley at roughly 2,100 metres. It is regularly described as one of the highest permanently inhabited places in Europe. Since 1996 it has been on the UNESCO World Heritage list as part of the Upper Svaneti site; what is protected is not a single monument but the whole historic pattern of settlement, with its towers, houses and hay meadows.

The view is the main event. Shkhara, Georgia's highest summit at 5,193 metres, rises directly behind the villages and closes the valley. On a low hill above Zhibiani stands Lamaria church, a small twelfth-century building with surviving frescoes and its own defensive tower. In Chazhashi an ethnographic museum displays icons, weapons and household objects.

Things worth knowing in advance:

  • In winter the village is often cut off — snow can close the road for weeks at a time
  • The final stretch from Mestia is unpaved and genuinely needs a high-clearance vehicle
  • Services are minimal — a handful of guesthouses, small cafes, no ATM

Ushguli is not a packaged attraction, and that is exactly its value. It remains a working village: people still keep cattle and cut hay on the same slopes their families worked more than a century ago, while visitors walk between the towers.

Practical advice

Leave Mestia in the morning, before 09:00 — it is two hours each way and you do not want to drive the gravel back in the dark. Walking the four villages takes two to three hours, plus about forty minutes for the climb to Lamaria church. Dress modestly inside the church: a headscarf and a long skirt for women. Park at the marked area by the village entrance and continue on foot, since the lanes are narrow and livestock wanders freely. Bring cash; toilets are in the cafes.

How to get there from Tbilisi

Ushguli is roughly 515 km from Tbilisi, which realistically means a two-day approach with a night in Mestia. From Mestia it is 45–47 km and about two hours: asphalt at first, then a gravel and stone road that crosses the river several times and deteriorates sharply after rain. That is precisely why a high-clearance vehicle is required here — a low car is neither safe nor covered by rental insurance on this section. The last fuel is in Mestia, so fill the tank before you set off, and check the weather, as heavy rain can make the fords slow.

Nearby places

Ski area

Hatsvali and Tetnuldi Ski Areas

Mestia's two ski zones — Hatsvali with sheltered forest runs, and Tetnuldi, where the lifts pass 3,000 metres.

Town

Mestia and the Svan Towers

Upper Svaneti's main town at 1,500 m — medieval stone defence towers, two strong museums and the trailhead for every route in the region.

Mountain

Chalaadi Glacier

The most accessible glacier near Mestia — a short drive up the valley and a two-hour walk to the ice tongue.
